title: Cruise coverage lowers the passive-transport mismatch off California from 9.4 to 3.8 micromol/kg on sigma0 26.5
abstract: We test whether fixed passive transport can fit published North Pacific oxygen histories on density 26.5. A linear program permits any nonnegative mixture of two western source histories with integer delays of 0-25 years and total weight at most one. For five-year windows centred in 1984-2020, the smallest maximum error is 9.399 micromol/kg off California, compared with 1.494-3.512 in three offshore regions. Requiring at least two cruises per source year lowers the California bound to 3.837, without changing the target data used in the test. Nine-year smoothing lowers it to 3.573. Removing only the one-cruise western year 2001 lowers the bound to 3.943. Thus a rejection at a five-micromol/kg tolerance is not robust to source coverage. The result does not show that this year is wrong or that passive transport is correct. It shows that a required added process cannot be inferred from these processed histories without a source-error bound. Saved primal and dual witnesses prove the main numerical optima. Limits include interpolation across gaps, regional proxies for flow boundaries, fixed delay weights and no joint observation-error model.
